facts.statement: Jeholopterus lived during the Middle to Late Jurassic in Inner Mongolia, China, and possibly the Early Cretaceous in North Korea.
facts.quote: Jeholopterus was a small anurognathid pterosaur known from the Middle to Late Jurassic Daohugou Beds of the Tiaojishan Formation of Inner Mongolia, China, and possibly the Early Cretaceous Sinuiju Formation of North Korea.

facts.statement: The genus Jeholopterus was named in 2002 by Wang Xiaolin, Zhou Zhonghe, and Xu Xing.
facts.quote: The genus was named in 2002 by Wang Xiaolin, Zhou Zhonghe and Xu Xing.

facts.statement: The genus name Jeholopterus combines the place of discovery, Jehol, with the Greek word for wing.
facts.quote: The genus name is derived from its place of discovery, Jehol in China, and a Latinized Greek pteron, "wing".

facts.statement: The species name ningchengensis refers to Ningcheng County.
facts.quote: The specific name refers to Ningcheng County.

facts.statement: The fossil preserves exquisite carbonized skin fibers and pycnofibres.
facts.quote: This includes exquisite preservation of carbonized skin fibers and pycnofibres.

facts.statement: A 2009 study by Alexander Kellner reported three layers of wing fibers that allowed the animal to adapt its wing profile.
facts.quote: In 2009 Alexander Kellner published a study reporting the presence of three layers of fibers in the wing, allowing the animal to precisely adapt the wing profile.

facts.statement: Jeholopterus had mostly small, peg-like teeth, though some were longer and recurved.
facts.quote: Most teeth are small and peg-like, but some are longer and recurved.

facts.statement: Jeholopterus had a short neck with seven or eight cervical vertebrae.
facts.quote: The neck was short with seven or eight cervical vertebrae.

facts.statement: Jeholopterus had robust wing bones and very short metacarpals.
facts.quote: The wing bones are robust. The metacarpals are very short.

facts.statement: Jeholopterus had a short pteroid bone that supported a propatagium pointing toward the body.
facts.quote: A short pteroid, supporting a propatagium, is pointing towards the body.

facts.statement: Jeholopterus possessed long, curved claws on its hands.
facts.quote: The hand claws are long and curved.

facts.statement: Jeholopterus had relatively elongated wings with a wingspan of ninety centimeters.
facts.quote: They are relatively elongated with a wingspan of ninety centimetres.

facts.statement: Jeholopterus had short but robust legs.
facts.quote: The legs are short but robust.

facts.statement: The elongated fifth toe suggests the presence of a membrane between the legs, the uropatagium.
facts.quote: The fifth toe is elongated, according to the authors supporting a membrane between the legs, the uropatagium.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the preserved wing tissue attached to the legs.
facts.quote: Wing tissue is preserved, though its extent is debatable, including the exact points of attachment to the legs (or if it is attached to the legs at all).

facts.statement: Researchers hypothesized that Jeholopterus might have been a piscivore because it was the largest known anurognathid.
facts.quote: Wang et al hypothesized that Jeholopterus, being the largest genus known of the group, might also have been a piscivore, a fish-eater.

facts.statement: Jeholopterus is classified within the family Anurognathidae.
facts.quote: Jeholopterus was by the authors assigned to the Anurognathidae.

facts.statement: Jeholopterus is a small anurognathid pterosaur from the Daohugou Beds of northeast China, preserved with skin and feather-like structures.
facts.quote: Jeholopterus es un género extinto de un pequeño pterosaurio anurognátido de los Lechos Daohugou del noreste de China (de edad incierta, probablemente del Jurásico Medio o Jurásico Superior), entre hace 168 a 152 millones de años), preservado con restos de piel y "plumas".

facts.statement: According to Wang et al., evidence suggests Jeholopterus's wings attached to the ankle.
facts.quote: Las alas de Jeholopterus muestran evidencia de que unían al tobillo, de acuerdo a Wang et al..

facts.statement: The paleoartist David Peters popularized unique interpretations of Jeholopterus without ever personally examining the fossil.
facts.quote: Aunque él nunca ha examinado el fósil por sí mismo, el artista publicitario y paleoartista David Peters ha popularizado sus opiniones idiosincrásicas acerca de Jeholopterus y otros pterosaurios a través de Internet.

facts.statement: In 2003, David Peters claimed to have discovered soft tissue remains, including a horse-like tail used as a flyswatter or distractor, using image manipulation software, a finding disputed by other researchers.
facts.quote: A través de la manipulación de imágenes descargadas de Jeholopterus en el programa de ordenador Photoshop, David Peters (2003) informa que él descubrió un juego único de restos de tejidos blandos, incluyendo una cola similar a la de un caballo que Peters especula que puede haber sido usada como un espantamoscas o un distractor

facts.statement: David Peters suggested that Jeholopterus was a vampire-like pterosaur with rattlesnake fangs and a reinforced palate adapted to pierce tough skin, though this methodology has been strongly criticized.
facts.quote: Peters también reportó que él halló "colmillos como de una serpiente de cascabel", y estos, junto a lo que él describió como una mandíbula similar a la de la víbora de cascabel, con paladar reforzado, ungueales "quirúrgicamente afilados", miembros robustos y otras características sugieren que Jeholopterus era un pterosaurio vampiro adaptado a hundir sus "colmillos" entre piel dura

facts.statement: Peters hypothesized that the small lower jaw teeth could not penetrate skin but could compress wounds like pincers.
facts.quote: Los pequeños dientes de la mandíbula inferior no podrían penetrar pero podrían comprimir la herida como unas tenazas.

facts.statement: Expert pterosaur researcher Chris Bennett described Peters' findings as a fantasy and vehemently denounced his methodology.
facts.quote: El destacado experto en pterosaurios Chris Bennett ha descrito los hallazgos de Peters como una "fantasía" y ha denunciado vehementemente su metodología.

facts.statement: Jeholopterus belongs to the parent group Anurognathidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Anurognathidae

facts.statement: The family of Jeholopterus is Anurognathidae.
facts.quote: Family: Anurognathidae

facts.statement: Jeholopterus is classified within the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Jeholopterus lived during the Callovian stage, between 165.3 and 161.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Callovian to Callovian (165.3 to 161.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: There is one recorded fossil occurrence of Jeholopterus in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 1
